question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-1R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z&=1 \\ y&=-3 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=-3-(0)(4)=-3 \\ x&=1-(2)(-3)-(1)(4)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 3,-3,4\rangle$.
